text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Three foreign companies have acquired stakes in Intercontinental Merchant Bank from an offer for sale of 150 million naira shares. The three are Britain's Blackstone Assets Management Trust and Petrocarbon Technologies, with American firm Blue Marine and Union Limited. Nigerian investors did not seem keen about the offer.
- Petroleum products marketing companies are being forced to counter a trend in declining sales particularly in profitable areas such as lubricants and chemicals.
- The government's Petroleum Trust Fund is to grant a loan for the transport of 200,000 tonnes of steel super concentrates abandoned at Itakpe to the Aladja Steel Company for processing into billets.
- Local councillors who want to be re-elected when multiparty elections are held will have to resign their seats.
- Local telephone firm Intercellular Nigeria may soon break the state telephone monopoly by introducing 20,000 new lines with a 480 million naira investment.
- Finance Minister Anthony Ani is on Wednesday expected to attend a forum to appraise reforms at Nigeria's ports and discuss budgetary expectations for 1997.
